passages.text: Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you—I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
I speak to you now.
I appeal to you.
I appeal by the mildness of Christ.
I appeal by the gentleness of Christ.
Christ is mild and gentle.
When I am with you face to face, I am humble.
When I am away from you, I am bold toward you.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐγὼ Παῦλος παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς διὰ τῆς πραΰτητος καὶ ἐπιεικείας τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὃς κατὰ πρόσωπον μὲν ταπεινὸς ἐν ὑμῖν ἀπὼν δὲ θαρρῶ εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul is humble when he is with them.
Paul is bold when he is away from them.
Paul appeals to the church by the gentleness and meekness of Christ.
Paul begs the church for something.
Paul asks that when he comes, he will not need to be bold.
Paul expects he might have to be bold toward some people.
Some people think Paul and his companions live according to the flesh.
Paul does not want to be bold toward those who presume this.
Paul hopes he will not need to act with such confidence against them.
passages.original: δέομαι δὲ τὸ μὴ παρὼν θαρρῆσαι τῇ πεποιθήσει ᾗ λογίζομαι τολμῆσαι ἐπί τινας τοὺς λογιζομένους ἡμᾶς ὡς κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦντας

passages.text: For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and his companions live as humans in this world.
They have physical bodies.
They do not fight their battles in a human way.
They do not use worldly methods to struggle or fight.
They do not wage war according to the flesh.
passages.original: Ἐν σαρκὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦντες οὐ κατὰ σάρκα στρατευόμεθα

passages.text: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the world. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
passages.sermon:
We are Christians.
We fight spiritual battles.
We do not use weapons from this world.
Our weapons come from God.
God makes our weapons powerful.
Our weapons can destroy strongholds.
passages.original: τὰ γὰρ ὅπλα τῆς στρατείας ἡμῶν οὐ σαρκικὰ ἀλλὰ δυνατὰ τῷ Θεῷ πρὸς καθαίρεσιν ὀχυρωμάτων

passages.text: We tear down arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
passages.sermon:
We are followers of Christ.
We fight spiritual battles.
We destroy arguments against God’s knowledge.
We tear down every proud thing that stands against God.
We capture every thought.
We make every thought obey Christ.
passages.original: λογισμοὺς καθαιροῦντες καὶ πᾶν ὕψωμα ἐπαιρόμενον κατὰ τῆς γνώσεως τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ αἰχμαλωτίζοντες πᾶν νόημα εἰς τὴν ὑπακοὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.
passages.sermon: We are ready to punish every act of disobedience.\r\nWe will do this when your obedience is complete.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχοντες ἐκδικῆσαι πᾶσαν παρακοήν ὅταν πληρωθῇ ὑμῶν ἡ ὑπακοή

passages.text: You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.
passages.sermon:
You look at outward appearances.
Some people feel sure that they belong to Christ.
If anyone feels sure about this, he should think carefully.
He should remember that we also belong to Christ, just as much as he does.
passages.original: Τὰ κατὰ πρόσωπον βλέπετε εἴ τις πέποιθεν ἑαυτῷ Χριστοῦ εἶναι τοῦτο λογιζέσθω πάλιν ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῦ ὅτι καθὼς αὐτὸς Χριστοῦ οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς

passages.text: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
The Lord gave Paul and his companions authority.
This authority comes from God.
God gave this authority to build up the church.
God did not give this authority to tear down the church.
Paul may speak boldly about this authority.
Even if Paul boasts more than usual about this authority, he will not be ashamed.
Paul uses this authority for your good.
Paul does not use this authority to harm you.
passages.original: ἐάν τε γὰρ περισσότερόν τι καυχήσωμαι περὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἡμῶν ἧς ἔδωκεν ὁ Κύριος εἰς οἰκοδομὴν καὶ οὐκ εἰς καθαίρεσιν ὑμῶν οὐκ αἰσχυνθήσομαι

passages.text: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of these letters.
Paul does not want to frighten the people.
Paul does not want people to think he tries to scare them with his letters.
passages.original: ἵνα μὴ δόξω ὡς ἂν ἐκφοβεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ τῶν ἐπιστολῶν

passages.text: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
passages.sermon:
Some people speak about Paul.
They say his letters are weighty.
They say his letters are forceful.
They say his physical presence is unimpressive.
They say his speaking is of no account.
passages.original: Ὅτι Αἱ ἐπιστολαὶ μέν φησίν Βαρεῖαι καὶ ἰσχυραί ἡ δὲ παρουσία τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενὴς καὶ ὁ λόγος ἐξουθενημένος

passages.text: Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nSome people criticize Paul.
\r\nThey say his letters are strong and forceful.
\r\nThey say his physical presence is weak.
\r\nThey say his speaking is unimpressive.
\r\nPaul addresses these people.
\r\nThese people should think carefully.
\r\nPaul is the same in his letters when he is absent.
\r\nPaul will be the same in his actions when he is present.
passages.original: τοῦτο λογιζέσθω ὁ τοιοῦτος ὅτι οἷοί ἐσμεν τῷ λόγῳ δι’ ἐπιστολῶν ἀπόντες τοιοῦτοι καὶ παρόντες τῷ ἔργῳ

passages.text: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul writes to the Corinthians.
Paul says, "We do not dare to classify ourselves with some people."
Some people commend themselves.
We do not compare ourselves with those people.
Those people measure themselves by their own standards.
Those people compare themselves with themselves.
Those people do not understand what they are doing.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ τολμῶμεν ἐνκρῖναι ἢ συνκρῖναι ἑαυτούς τισιν τῶν ἑαυτοὺς συνιστανόντων ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἑαυτοὺς μετροῦντες καὶ συνκρίνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς οὐ συνιᾶσιν

passages.text: We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Christ.
We do not boast beyond our limits.
We only boast within the field God has given us.
God assigned this field to us.
This field of influence reaches to you.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς δὲ οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχησόμεθα ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τοῦ κανόνος οὗ ἐμέρισεν ἡμῖν ὁ Θεὸς μέτρου ἐφικέσθαι ἄχρι καὶ ὑμῶν

passages.text: We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian church.
Paul and his companions brought the gospel of Christ to the Corinthians first.
Paul says, “We are not overstepping our bounds.”
Paul and his companions did not act as if they had never come to the Corinthians.
Paul and his companions reached the Corinthians with the gospel of Christ before anyone else did.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ὡς μὴ ἐφικνούμενοι εἰς ὑμᾶς ὑπερεκτείνομεν ἑαυτούς ἄχρι γὰρ καὶ ὑμῶν ἐφθάσαμεν ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well, so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.
passages.sermon:
We do not boast about work done by others.
We do not claim credit for things outside our own area.
We hope your faith will grow.
As your faith grows, our work among you will also grow.
We want our area of influence to become greater among you.
We want to preach the gospel in places beyond you.
We do not want to boast about work already finished in someone else’s area.
passages.original: οὐκ εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα καυχώμενοι ἐν ἀλλοτρίοις κόποις ἐλπίδα δὲ ἔχοντες αὐξανομένης τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ἐν ὑμῖν μεγαλυνθῆναι κατὰ τὸν κανόνα ἡμῶν εἰς περισσείαν εἰς τὰ ὑπερέκεινα ὑμῶν εὐαγγελίσασθαι οὐκ ἐν ἀλλοτρίῳ κανόνι εἰς τὰ ἕτοιμα καυχήσασθαι

passages.text: Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
Paul gives instructions about boasting.
Anyone who wants to boast must boast in the Lord.
No one should boast in themselves.
Boast only in what the Lord has done.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ καυχώμενος ἐν Κυρίῳ καυχάσθω

passages.text: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
passages.sermon: God approves people.\r\nGod does not approve people who praise themselves.\r\nGod approves people whom He Himself praises.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ὁ ἑαυτὸν συνιστάνων ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν δόκιμος ἀλλὰ ὃν ὁ Κύριος συνίστησιν
